heading: Convert WebM recordings to MP4
introduction: Convert a supported WebM recording into H.264 MP4 with AAC audio when present. Original display dimensions are preserved, and your selected recording stays on your device.

sections.heading: Convert in three steps
sections.body:
1. Select a WebM file and wait for validation.
2. Review the fixed MP4 output and choose Convert to MP4.
3. Download the result, then play the picture and sound before replacing your source.

sections.heading: What the converter changes
sections.body: The output is an MP4 container with H.264 video and AAC audio when an audio track is present. Compatible H.264 video may be kept without re-encoding; other supported video codecs are encoded as H.264. This is an actual conversion, not an extension rename. Subtitles and cover art are not retained.

sections.heading: Dimensions and file size
sections.body: The converter preserves source display dimensions. It has no image-size target or resolution selector. A compatible MP4 may be larger than its WebM source; that is reported as a conversion, not a compression saving. Use the video compressor for supported MP4/MOV compression settings.

sections.heading: Time and input limits
sections.body: Inputs can be up to 200 MiB each, within the 500-file and 300 MiB queue limits. The first media job downloads the browser engine. Duration, resolution, codec and device speed affect processing, and each media job has a five-minute processing limit. Long or complex recordings can fail within the file-size limit.

faq.q: Can I choose another output format?
faq.a: This converter has fixed MP4 output with H.264 video and AAC audio when present. It does not offer a format menu.

faq.q: Why is my MP4 larger than the WebM?
faq.a: A new container and codec can require more bytes. The tool reports the actual result and does not present growth as a saving.

faq.q: Can I rename WebM to MP4 instead?
faq.a: No. Changing a filename does not change the container or encoded video. Use a real converter and check playback.
